title: The Garden of the Crescent Cove
premise: August Nystrom, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in scandal a decade ago, hires a stranger—Marisol Vega, a waitress with a fake smile and a real fugitive past—to pose as his girlfriend at his family's island reunion. As the weekend deepens, August discovers Marisol is hiding from a man she testified against, and his family's reunion is secretly a trap set by that same man, who is August's estranged brother-in-law. To protect Marisol, August must finally speak the confession he has rehearsed for ten years, exposing the truth of what happened the night his fiancée left, and together they turn the reunion itself into the stage where justice—outside any courtroom—gets done. The book ends with Marisol's name cleared and August, for the first time, planning a wedding he believes in: their own, small and real, at the crescent cove.
about_author: Cyrus Eastwick is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent seven years staging other people's happily-ever-afters before turning to fiction. He writes love stories about people who have excellent reasons not to fall in love.

chapters.title: Tiers and Tulle
chapters.summary: August's POV. While directing a lavish wedding he secretly disdains, August receives his mother's summons to the family's tenth-annual reunion at Crescent Cove—where his ex-fiancée's family will be present. Emotional beat: weary control masking old dread; he decides he'd rather invent a girlfriend than arrive alone.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Said Yes to Strangers
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A waitress at August's venue, Marisol is counting cash under an assumed name, one step ahead of a man she once testified against. When the fastidious wedding planner awkwardly offers her money to play his girlfriend, she sees a weekend of safety in plain sight. Emotional beat: guarded pragmatism meeting an unexpected door out.

chapters.title: Contract of Small Lies
chapters.summary: August's POV. Over coffee, they negotiate rules: invented meet-cute, no real names, no real feelings. August rehearses his cover story; Marisol is suspiciously good at improvisation. Emotional beat: playful chemistry crackling under mutual distrust—each recognizes a fellow person hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: Arrivals at the Cove
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The reunion begins: a cliffside house, nosy aunts, and August's polished sister Claire—whose husband, Damian Voss, greets Marisol with a recognition that chills her. She realizes the reunion is no accident of geography. Emotional beat: the fake romance must become convincing fast, because a real threat has just shaken her hand.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: August's POV. Between toasts and a chaotic kitchen rescue, August and Marisol's staged affection stops feeling staged; a dance on the terrace turns honest. But he glimpses Damian watching Marisol too closely, and his sister's marriage suddenly looks like a cage. Emotional beat: the dangerous warmth of believing your own lie.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Cornered on the beach, Damian reveals he knows exactly who she is—and that Claire's reunion invitation was his design, bait to draw out the witness who ruined him. He gives her until Sunday to disappear quietly. Emotional beat: terror crystallizing into resolve; she decides to stop running.

chapters.title: The Confession Rehearsed for a Decade
chapters.summary: August's POV. Marisol tells August everything, and his protective fury cracks open his own buried truth: the scandal that ended his engagement was him covering for Damian's fraud—and his silence bought his family's comfort at the cost of his integrity. Emotional beat: shame transformed into purpose; he begins drafting the sentence he's rehearsed for ten years.

chapters.title: Sunday, Before the Toasts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Damian moves to force Marisol out early; August secretly records Damian's threats and Claire, tipped off, finds proof her husband forged the documents Marisol once testified about. Emotional beat: rising tension as allies assemble in whispers while Damian works the room, confident and untouchable.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the reunion's final dinner, August stands to toast—and instead delivers his decade-rehearsed confession: the truth of Damian's crimes, his own complicity, and Marisol's innocence. Damian lunges, but the recording and Claire's testimony land him in the hands of waiting authorities. Emotional beat: catharsis; the price of survival finally paid in full, and worth it.

chapters.title: A Wedding He Believes In
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, closing on both. Weeks later, Marisol's name is cleared; Claire begins again, freer than before. On the sand at Crescent Cove, August—wedding planner, believer at last—asks Marisol not to play a role but to write a real one with him. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope; love kept in the present tense at last.
